compiled_state.title: [pr-comment-response]: deferred-comment title uses first 100 chars of body -> uninformative titles like 'PR comment deferred:'
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** c00899e0b7252b6a54aad558499917f0548c3524
* **component:** plugins/dso/scripts/pr-comment-response.sh line 369

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

A deferred PR-comment ticket title should provide enough signal to triage the ticket without opening it — minimally including the PR number and a meaningful slug or summary of the deferred concern.

#### Actual Behavior

The title is hardcoded as \`PR comment deferred: \${short_body}\` where \`short_body\` is the first 100 chars of the raw GitHub comment body. Real-world samples observed in Jira before deletion 2026-05-14:

* \`PR comment deferred:\` (4 occurrences — original comment started with whitespace/punctuation)
* \`PR comment deferred: Agreed, we should track this separately.\` (4 occurrences — generic agreement-to-defer, no domain signal)

Neither variant tells a reader what the deferred concern was. The ticket is unactionable without opening it.

### 3. Action History

Discovered while reconciling Jira open issues against local open tickets — 8 PR-deferred Jira issues with these titles were deleted in a cleanup pass.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* plugins/dso/scripts/pr-comment-response.sh:369 — title construction
* /dso:respond-to-pr-comments — caller

Suggested fix: title should include PR number and a slug derived from the deferred concern (not the agreement-to-defer reply). The classifier already separates accept/defend/defer; the source of the deferral (the reviewer's original comment, not the agent's "Agreed" reply) should drive the title.
